- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) and underestimate in bearish (sentiment < 0.3), especially after recent spikes.
- Model tends to overshoot after sharp upward moves in history (e.g., 73+), then fails to correct downward — apply mean reversion bias to next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is low (0.0–0.3) and price drops, model often undercorrects — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often dips 1–3 days after model’s peak, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.27–0.53 cycles, model tends to overfit recent trends — dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% in next 7–14 days.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps >0.77 but price doesn’t follow, reduce forecast sensitivity by 30% for next 5 days.
